description: Add, remove, disable, enable, or move a firewall rule on a MikroTik router, in the filter, nat or raw table, IPv4 (family ip, the default) or IPv6 (family ipv6). Matches addresses, ports, protocol, interfaces, interface lists, and connection/NAT state; nat rules take toAddresses/toPorts (e.g. a dst-nat port forward), jump rules need jumpTarget, reject rules may set rejectWith. Uses comment as idempotency key for deduplication and identification: a repeated add returns already_exists only when the match, NAT targets, jump target, reject reply, and disabled state agree, otherwise CONFLICT (use enable/disable when only the disabled state differs). move takes ruleId and destination (a rule .id to place it before, or end) instead of chain/ruleAction/comment, and returns no_change when the rule is already there; dynamic rules cannot be moved. Supports dry-run mode. Every real write is guarded by a dead-man switch (autoRevertSeconds, default 60): a RouterOS scheduler job that undoes the change is armed first and removed only once the router answers a new REST connection afterwards, so a rule that locks out management reverts itself.

action.description: Action to perform: add, remove, disable, or enable a rule (found by comment), or move a rule (by ruleId) before another

autoRevertSeconds.description: Dead-man switch: before the write, arm a RouterOS scheduler job that undoes it after this many seconds; it is removed once the router answers a new REST connection after the change. 0 turns it off. Default 60

chain.description: Firewall chain, required except for move (e.g. input, forward, output, srcnat, dstnat; raw: prerouting, output)

comment.description: Comment to identify the rule (used as idempotency key); omit for none

confirmationToken.description: Token from a prior APPROVAL_REQUIRED response. Re-submit the identical call with this token to confirm the destructive action.

connectionNatState.description: Connection NAT state to match, e.g. dstnat or !dstnat

connectionState.description: Connection-tracking states, comma-separated, optionally negated: established,related or !invalid

destination.description: Where to move the rule: the .id of the rule to place it before, or end for the bottom of the table; move only

disabled.description: Whether the rule should be disabled

dryRun.description: If true, validate and return planned changes without applying

family.description: Address family: ip (IPv4, /ip firewall) or ipv6 (/ipv6 firewall)

inInterfaceList.description: Incoming interface list, e.g. WAN or !LAN

jumpTarget.description: Chain to jump to; required with ruleAction jump and rejected otherwise

outInterfaceList.description: Outgoing interface list, e.g. WAN or !LAN

placeBefore.description: Place the new rule before this rule ID

protocol.description: Protocol to match; ICMP is icmp for family ip and icmpv6 for family ipv6

rejectWith.description: ICMP or TCP reply for ruleAction reject only. ip: icmp-network-unreachable (default), icmp-host-unreachable, icmp-port-unreachable, icmp-protocol-unreachable, icmp-network-prohibited, icmp-host-prohibited, icmp-admin-prohibited, tcp-reset. ipv6: icmp-no-route (default), icmp-admin-prohibited, icmp-not-neighbour, icmp-address-unreachable, icmp-port-unreachable, tcp-reset

routerId.description: Router ID; omit to use the default router.

ruleAction.description: RouterOS rule action, required except for move (e.g. accept, drop, reject, jump, masquerade; raw also notrack)

ruleId.description: Rule to move, by its RouterOS .id (e.g. *1A, from the list tool); move only

table.description: Firewall table to manage: filter, nat or raw

toAddresses.description: NAT target address or range (nat table only, e.g. dst-nat)

toPorts.description: NAT target port or range (nat table only)

name: manage_firewall_rule
title: Manage Firewall Rule
